newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Survey finds Australian CFOs upwardly mobile.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Survey finds Australian CFOs upwardly mobile.

text.p: Changing jobs is one of the best ways to get ahead if you are the chief financial officer (CFO) of an Australian company, according to a recent survey of CFOs.
The survey, conducted by executive search group Korn/Ferry International, was sent to 350 CFOs in Australia's top 300 private and public firms and got a response rate of 70 percent.
"The day of the faithful Dickensian bookkeeper, poring for decades over his legers, has gone," said David Benn, Korn/Ferry's managing director.
The survey found 90 percent of CFOs considered strategic job changes to be one of the key elements in achieving success.
Two thirds of CFOs surveyed had spent less than five years in their present position and two thirds less than 10 years in their current organisation.
"The good news is that this provides a cross pollination of ideas and forces career orientated professionals to keep up to date with the changing demands of their profession," Benn said.
Korn/Ferry said the typical CFO is an Australian born, 45 year old male with a university degree.
Only four percent of respondents were female and all of these were under the age of 45.
The survey found that a majority of CFOs saw their current position as a way station with 45 percent aspiring to be a chief executive officer (CEO) and 18 percent a professional director.

Australian CFOs have no shortage of exposure to the power seats within an organisation, the survey finding 96 percent of CFO had regular access to the CEO and three quarters had regular dialogue with the board.
